rubrics.criterion: The logic that decides which bar pattern of the EAN digit record to emit at a given content position (left-hand odd, left-hand even, or right-hand) is defined on or behind the digit record type itself, and no helper whose own state is just a field copied from that record family performs that selection anymore.
rubrics.rationale: The EAN-13 encoding loop of this repo had its variant selection moved behind a private helper seeded with the lead digit's pattern; the maintainer prompt explicitly asks that digit facts be decided by the record that owns the patterns, so a repair that leaves the selection inside such a helper (or re-inlines it into the looping consumer) has not resolved this instance's misplaced placement.

rubrics.criterion: The QR rendering routine and the data-region padding routine both take the final matrix dimension and the data-region byte capacity from code defined on (or exposing) the version layout record, and no stateless side type re-derives those two quantities from the version records' raw block-layout fields.
rubrics.rationale: Both QR consumers in this instance switched to a planner that owns no data and reads the version tables' raw fields; the requested outcome is that geometry and capacity facts be supplied by the data owner, whether through the pre-existing descriptive methods or through new owner-defined ones, so the criterion checks that placement, not a specific name or shape.

rubrics.criterion: The Data Matrix error-correction pass obtains its per-block data budget and per-block error-correction budget from code defined on (or exposing) the symbol size profile, instead of computing region geometry and codeword budgets in the error-correction method itself from the profile's raw fields.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's ECC method re-opened the size profile and restated its accounting inline, special cases included, while the layout pass kept using the profile's accessors, leaving the profile's rules stated in two places; the prompt asks for the budgeting facts to be supplied by the profile side of that boundary.

rubrics.criterion: Every internal call site of the relocated behavior was rewired in the same patch: the EAN-13 encoding loop builds no per-code helper object anymore, and the QR render routine and padding routine obtain their numbers through the same owner-supplied surface without leaving any caller of a removed symbol behind.
rubrics.rationale: The three relocations in this instance each have consumers inside hot encoding paths (the digit-position loop, all eight mask candidate builds, the capacity pad loop); a move that updates helpers but leaves a consumer calling the old shape would not compile or would silently keep the old computation, so the follow-through itself is gradeable.

rubrics.criterion: No repair introduces a state where two code paths independently re-state the same symbol fact, such as a consumer that keeps its inlined budget/geometry derivation while also calling the owner, or a freshly introduced wrapper that just forwards to the other path's new method.
rubrics.rationale: The specific half-done outcome for this instance is a repaired owner boundary with the pre-existing derivation left alive at the consumer, which reproduces exactly the duplicated-accounting problem the maintainer describes while appearing to add an owner API.

rubrics.criterion: Types, constructors and methods that existed only to serve the removed derivations are deleted from the touched packages, so nothing in the datamatrix, qr or ean package remains defined but unreferenced as a consequence of the move.
rubrics.rationale: This instance planted an owner-less stateless planning type and a per-code helper with a constructor and a seeded field, both of which become dead weight once their behavior returns to the data owners; the prompt explicitly asks for scaffolding that becomes unnecessary to be removed rather than left behind.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not add new pass-through types, constructors or forwarding methods whose only content is a call to the relocated behavior, trading the removed scaffolding for differently named scaffolding in the same packages.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible failure mode for this instance is replacing the seeded digit helper or the frame-planning type with an equivalently owner-less facade that quotes the prompt's vocabulary while keeping the knowledge exactly where it started.

rubrics.criterion: The data budget used per block for the 144x144 symbol profile is still 156 codewords for blocks 0 through 7 and 155 codewords for the remaining blocks, whether the special case is preserved in the owning code or delegated to an accessor that already encodes it.
rubrics.rationale: This is the one profile in this repo whose blocks do not split evenly; the existing suite exercises the ECC pass on smaller symbols only, so silently flattening the special case into an average would pass the tests while corrupting layout on the largest size, and the maintainer prompt calls this trap out by name.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not alter which variant a left-hand EAN-13 digit receives: positions 1 through 6 must still be keyed by the corresponding rows of the lead digit's parity pattern (odd variant when false, even variant when true in this codebase's tables) and positions 7 through 12 must still use the right-hand pattern.
rubrics.rationale: Moving digit selection in this instance almost always touches the parity lookup; an off-by-one at position 1 or a swapped odd/even condition would compile, pass module tests lazily, and produce readable-looking but incorrectly encoded EAN-13 symbols, which is the concrete silent failure this instance is exposed to.

rubrics.criterion: The QR capacity path still pads and terminates every bitstream to exactly the same total: the owners' data-region byte count multiplied by eight bits per version and error-correction level, with no byte/bit confusion and no truncation when a bitstream needs only the four-bit terminator.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's padding routine and render routine consumed two different quantities from one helper call; if byte capacity and module geometry get swapped or re-based during the move, codes whose payload nearly fills the region can silently gain or lose data bytes for specific versions while ordinary inputs still encode fine.

rubrics.criterion: The exported surface of every touched package is unchanged: the existing Encode/EncodeWithColor functions keep their signatures and behavior, and no identifier introduced by the repair is exported.
rubrics.rationale: The maintainer prompt for this instance fixes the compatibility boundary at the exported API of the module; internal types are free to move, so any newly exported name or signature change marks scope creep out of the agreed boundary rather than a style issue.
